objective: async/await syntax and error handling with try/catch
secondaryObjectives: The event loop, call stack, and task queue (conceptual model)

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: 'forEach() expects a synchronous function — it does not wait for promises. Make sure you are aware of the implications while using promises (or async functions) as forEach callbacks', with an example whose naive expected output is 14 and actual output 0. The page points to promise composition for sequential or parallel async work.

Lakeside Pantry, its volunteers, shifts and deadline are invented teaching values; console and test output are authored renderings. That a try/catch around forEach cannot catch a rejection from an async callback, and that an empty .catch() handler discards the error, follow from forEach not awaiting its callbacks (the source above) and from how promise rejection works; Promise.all rejecting with the first rejection is standard behavior, stated here as the author's and not read on a page for this round.

The test suite can mock api.save to reject chosen shifts.

writeup.question: For the team: why volunteers were told their shifts were saved, what you changed, and how you know.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: forEach calls the async callback for each shift and returns at once; it does not wait for the promises, so the toast runs before any save settles, and a rejection inside a callback is uncaught. Not the server.
parts.modelAnswer: forEach does not await; the toast lied and the 409s went uncaught.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: Await each save (for...of) or the composed promise, with try/catch, and report what failed. A try/catch around forEach catches nothing from the callbacks; an empty .catch() handler hides the failures; Promise.all reports a failure but not which shifts.
parts.modelAnswer: for...of with await and a per-save try/catch; the failures shown by shift.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: A test with mocked rejections, after the last change: the failed shifts are named, and no success message appears before the saves settle.

scoring.modelReasoning: forEach expects a synchronous callback and does not wait for promises, so saveAll() shows 'All 12 shifts saved' before any save settles, and a rejection inside a callback is uncaught. A try/catch around the forEach finishes before any callback rejects, and an empty .catch() handler silences the failures. Await each save in a for...of loop with try/catch, collect what failed and show it by shift; Promise.all in try/catch catches the failure but cannot say which shifts. Prove it with a test that mocks rejections for two shifts.
